notes.iddi: L’Aïd; Aïd Moubarak ! is also common.
notes.alizaliwa: Il est né, elle est née.

guidebook.intro: Talk about faith, prayer and religious holidays, with the blessings and greetings that go with them.

tips.title: Joyeux Noël, bonne fête de l’Aïd
body: Holiday greetings: **Joyeux Noël !**, **Joyeuses Pâques !**, **Bonne fête de l’Aïd !** (or **Aïd Moubarak !**), **Bon ramadan !** Holidays are **fêtes**, and a public holiday is **un jour férié**.

tips.title: Que Dieu te bénisse
body: Blessings start with **que** and use a special verb form, the subjunctive: **Que Dieu te bénisse !** (may God bless you). You’ll meet the subjunctive again later; for now, learn the phrase.
Born: **être né(e)**: **Je suis né à Kampala. Mamie est née à Zanzibar.**

culture.title: A land of many faiths
body: Francophone Africa is home to Christians, Muslims and traditional religions, often within one family. It’s common to wish your neighbours a good feast whatever their faith.
